about: WHO SAYS WHAT IN THEIR OWN TONGUE. Made 7 Oct 2026 by the builder of the turning line, for the people of the places files (Data/places/<port>.json). Every word and every line named here is one of story/tongues_793.json: nothing is added to that file's stock and nothing is invented. What is this file's own choice is only WHO is given WHICH: the tongues file says of each line who would say it, and the rules below follow that. A rule fits a person by id ('person'), or by role and people ('role', 'people': lists; a missing one fits all). The first rule that fits and has a 'hail' gives the word the person greets with: [tongue, word]. The first rule that fits and has a 'line' gives their one true line, which comes up in its own tongue and turns into English; 'on' names the line key it is said at (a person without that key says it at the first greeting). A line the tongues file marks as quoted from memory (check) or as not yet spoken in the year is passed over. Frisians: nothing in Frisian is written down before the thirteenth century, so a Frisian gets no whole line of his own; he hails with the Frisian word for what you are, kapmon, which the tongues file gives with that caveat. Franks and Saxons: every Frankish and Saxon line the tongues file has that a layman would say is later than 793, so they have a hail and no line. Churchmen speak Latin for holy things whatever their people. Edit freely.
